reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight emerges from treating each runner's performance history as a noisy observation along an underlying deterministic age-performance curve. By aggregating multiple such curves, one can estimate a probabilistic distribution of typical performance decline. This is achieved through mixed-effects modeling where fixed effects capture general trends and random effects account for inter-individual variation. The longitudinal nature allows for robust estimation even when individual runners drop out or retire. The separation into male/female trajectories enables gender-specific inference while maintaining comparability. The key failure mode arises when data sparsity limits reliable estimation of early-life or late-life performance, particularly for runners with short participation histories. The method avoids reliance on arbitrary world record benchmarks, instead grounding inference in observed runner behavior over time.
